summary: PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19 extracts Gao–Habegger, Heights in families of abelian varieties and the Geometric Bogomolov Conjecture (Ann. of Math. 189 (2019) 527–604; arXiv 1801.05762v3, hash reproduced; the published PDF, hash reproduced, was collated at every finding). It has 76 items, 9 routes and 27 source issues. I re-read the whole paper. The item statements are faithful, E1–E27 are correct, and no route lands in a finished blueprint. There are nine findings: 3 medium and 6 low. (1) The queue plans the Part IIs under different ids from the ones the routes use. Route 6 (the Betti map and Theorem 5.1) merges into DESIGN-AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII, whose first proposal is Kings–Sprang's Poincaré bundle, so under the queue's 'plan the first' rule the Betti-map tranche can be deferred. Theorem 1.4 (route 9) depends on it. This is the mechanism of RT-PAPER-BENOIST-19/1. (2) Item 15 is marked planned at R11.1, but R11.1 does not plan what the proof of Theorem 5.1 uses from BLR §7.5 Prop. 3: good reduction of A/A₀ and the exact sequence of abelian schemes. (3) Route 5 sends Lemma B.2 to IG.0, although its proof needs Riemann existence, which IG.3 plans downstream of IG.0. The paper's two uses of Riemann existence have no item. (4) Three slips are noted in item notes or corrected silently, but not recorded in sourceIssues: Remark 4.2 'endomorphism', Lemma 5.6's Hom ∩ Hom without monodromy equivariance, and 'Ax's Theorem [2]' for [3]. (5) Lemma 5.2 claims γ(0) ∈ Γ and a(0) ∈ ℤⁿ 'by looking at the proof of' Habegger–Pila Cor. 7.2(iii). That proof keeps only π₂(β(0)) ∈ π₂(Σ) after its final reparametrisation. The review wrote the stronger claim into item 30. A one-line repair uses (iii) as stated. (6) Several general analytic and topological inputs have no item: invariance of domain, the constant-rank theorem, closed subgroups of Tⁿ, the local theory of irreducible analytic spaces, and good covers. (7) Three library citations are missing: Mathlib's Blichfeldt principle, Dedekind flatness, and absLogHeight₁. (8) The prerequisites omit Ax 1972, Grothendieck 1966 and Koizumi 1976. (9) There is no sourceVersions field, and source.readSections still says the published version was not collated.

Disclosure. This session red-teamed Xie–Yuan 22 (PR #4694), Tsimerman 18 (PR #4903) and Lawrence–Venkatesh 20 (PR #4763). Finding /2 is related to RT-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/1, the characteristic-p failure of 'Zariski closure of an abelian subvariety is an abelian subscheme'. Here the characteristic is 0 and the gap is a different one, a status claim at R11.1. Finding /7's absLogHeight₁ citation repeats, for another item, the library observation of RT-PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18/9. Finding /1 relies on the mechanism established by RT-PAPER-BENOIST-19/1 (not my work, confirmed). No finding repeats my LD.6 or MPT Part II ownership findings (RT-PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18/1, /5, /10; RT-PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20/2). Items 30 and 31 are Habegger–Pila semi-rational counting and Ax 1972 for a constant abelian variety. They are routed to LD.6 as sources, which is the pattern RT-PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18/10 recommended.

Versions (30 September 2026). https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.05762v3 has SHA-256 ffe408dc6ba034b2a635488600decace1e89d61ad04860c391bef9409f2fd34e, as recorded. The arXiv abstract page lists v1 (17 January 2018), v2 (7 January 2019) and v3 (28 January 2019), so v3 is the latest. The published PDF https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v189-n2-p03-s.pdf (HTTP 200) has SHA-256 09304f589d44e7c44b050448bcc3317680e4954a47cad126762350e6e9a13bfd, which is the review's hash. The Annals article page gives 'Received: 19 January 2018, Revised: 10 October 2018' and links no correction. Crossref for 10.4007/annals.2019.189.2.3 has no update-to, updated-by or relation, and the filter updates:10.4007/annals.2019.189.2.3 returns 0 works.

The whole paper, read personally through pdftotext of arXiv v3 (§§1–11, Appendices A–C, references), with page images where layout mattered (p.25). Every new finding was collated with the published text. Re-derived or re-checked: Lemma 5.2's height bound (5.1) and the count 2^t; Proposition 5.3's two cases, including uniqueness and rationality of t in case (1); Proposition 5.4's transport; Lemma 5.8's induction, including the relative-dimension-0 subcases (E8); Theorem 5.1's general case, including why ϕ(U) consists of degenerate points (the Betti fibre through a degenerate point is a full disc over Δ, so its image is positive-dimensional); Lemma 6.2; Lemmas 6.3–6.6 (case (ii) dimension count); Proposition 6.7's induction; Proposition 6.9; Lemma 7.1 and Proposition 7.2 (adjugate bound, Blichfeldt shift); Lemma 8.2 (m = 2 + m₁ + m₂ = 2g; δ₀(0) ≠ 0 from Proposition 6.1(v)); §8.3 and Proposition 8.1 (dim Y′ ≥ 1, hence k ≤ n − 1); Lemma 9.2; the degree count 4^{N dim X}/(c₂δ4^N)^{dim X−1} = c′4^N in Proposition 9.1; Proposition 10.1's constants; the induction (10.4); Theorem 11.1's normalisations; Lemma C.2's dimension counts; Appendix A.3's contrapositive through Zhang's inequalities.

All 76 items were compared with the text at their locators, including hypotheses (g ≥ 1, dim S = 1, F ⊆ ℂ algebraically closed, the ranges d ≥ g − 1 and d ≥ max{1, g − dim B}, ℓ > D^{2^{g+1}(g+1)}). The review's corrections to items 3, 6, 22, 23, 25, 30, 31, 41, 44, 45, 57, 59, 63, 71 and 74 and the new item 76 were checked. Item 6's corrected kernel τ(A^{K̄/k}(k)) + A_tor and item 76's Koizumi bound n ≥ 3 are right. Item 40 silently states the monodromy-equivariant form (finding /4), and item 30's added sentence is finding /5. No other item misstates its source.

All 27 sourceIssues were checked at their locators in both versions. E18's example is right: P = (t, √(t³ − t)) on the constant curve y² = x³ − x is a non-constant K̄-point, so ĥ(P) > 0. E19's counterexample f(Q, s) = (Q + s·c(Q), s) is right: its leaves are holomorphic but not horizontal, while the Albanese-coordinate b is the true Betti map. E20, E22, E23 and E25 were re-derived. E27's three published headings were confirmed ('3.1. Proposition 2.1 implies Proposition 1.3', 'End of the proof of Theorem 4.1', 'Verification of (v) in Proposition 5.1'). E11 was confirmed half-corrected in print ('Z may no longer'). research/errata/REGISTER.md lists the paper once (§ at its line 7751). No other record duplicates these mistakes.

Habegger–Pila, arXiv 1409.0771v1 (the only arXiv version; SHA-256 ec372a109d64c81ca0b636f55f210029a04971da33b563fdcfec9d763897bf87), §7: Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.2 and its proof (p. 25), for items 30 and 32. The Ann. Sci. ÉNS text was not obtained; numdam served only a 6-page cover.

findings.claim: Routes 6 and 7 name the Part II roadmaps AbelianSchemesBettiMapsPartII and DegeneratingHodgeStructures. Route 9's brief imports 'Betti maps and Theorem 5.1 from AbelianSchemesBettiMapsPartII', and route 7's brief exports 'to AbelianSchemesBettiMapsPartII'. The queue never creates these ids. paper_designs groups every accepted part-ii route by its parent alone and creates DESIGN-AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuliPartII and DESIGN-HodgeStructuresPartII instead. It tells each merged job to 'plan the first here and record a restructure proposal for the rest' when the proposals split into independent directions. The first member of the abelian-scheme group, in registry order, is Kings–Sprang's 'universal vector extension and the completed Poincaré bundle' (PAPER-KINGS-SPRANG-25 route 2). Then come DGH21 route 5, this route 6 (the Betti map), Lipnowski–Tsimerman's 'finite-field isogeny classes' and GGK26 route 5. So the Betti-map tranche, which is three papers' joint proposal, can legitimately be deferred. But Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 1.1, which route 9 plans, rest on Theorem 5.1 through Lemma 6.2. The review accepted route 6 because it is 'shared with DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 and GAO-GE-KUHNE-26', but the queue ignores the id. The Hodge group (first member Landesman–Litt, 'variations, period maps') and the heights group (first member YUAN-26, uniform Bogomolov) have the first member in route 7's and route 9's own direction. The mechanism is RT-PAPER-BENOIST-19/1 (confirmed). This finding is its instance for this paper, not a new mechanism.

findings.claim: Item 15 states two things. The first is the Néron mapping property for an abelian scheme over a Dedekind base. The second is that 'for an abelian subvariety A₀ of the generic fibre, the Néron model of A/A₀ is an abelian scheme ℬ with an exact sequence 0 → A₀-model → 𝒜 → ℬ → 0 (BLR §1.2 Prop. 8, §7.5 Prop. 3)'. The item marks both as planned at R11.1. R11.1 plans existence and uniqueness of Néron models, the mapping property, extension of homomorphisms and the comparison of good reduction with an abelian-scheme model. It does not plan the second statement. That statement says the subvariety and the quotient of an abelian variety with good reduction have good reduction, and that their Néron models form an exact sequence of abelian schemes. R11.5 plans only Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and invariance of good reduction under isogeny. The proof of Theorem 5.1 (general case) also uses the Néron model 𝒞 of a Poincaré complement C and embeds it: 'we may assume 𝒞 ⊆ 𝒜'. In characteristic 0 this holds because the kernel of 𝒞 → 𝒜 is a finite étale group scheme, trivial on the generic fibre. In characteristic p it can fail, by the α_p mechanism of RT-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22/1. No layer states either fact, and the second half of item 15 is missing, not planned.
findings.evidence: Source, v3 p.29 (published p.561): 'By [8, Proposition 3 §7.5], the Néron model B of A/A0 is an abelian scheme over S and sits in the short exact sequence of abelian schemes over S 0 → A^{C(S)/C} × S → A → B → 0.' and 'Let C be the Néron model of C. It is an abelian scheme over S and we may assume C ⊆ A. The restriction ϕ|C : C → B is dominant and proper, hence surjective.' Atlas: R11.1's text (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.json) reads 'Construct Néron models … Prove uniqueness and functorial extension of homomorphisms. Identify the global invariant-differential lattice … Compare good reduction with an abelian-scheme model.' R11.5's text reads 'Prove Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich … Establish preservation of good reduction under isogeny.' Neither mentions subvarieties, quotients or exact sequences of Néron models. No NeronModels packet exists, and the queue has BP-NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties pending.
findings.fix: Split item 15. Keep (a) 'an abelian scheme over a Dedekind scheme is the Néron model of its generic fibre; the mapping property' as planned at R11.1. Add (b), status missing, routed as a source to NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1 (with R11.5 for the good-reduction step): 'Let 𝒜 be an abelian scheme over a Dedekind scheme S with generic fibre A, and A₀ ⊆ A an abelian subvariety. Then A₀ and A/A₀ have good reduction. Their Néron models 𝒜₀ and ℬ are abelian schemes, and 0 → 𝒜₀ → 𝒜 → ℬ → 0 is exact (BLR §7.5 Prop. 3). If all residue fields have characteristic 0, the extension 𝒜₀ → 𝒜 of the inclusion is a closed immersion.' Cite (b) in item 28's note. When FIX-RT-PAPER-XIE-YUAN-22 is applied, have that paper's good-reduction-model item import the same node, so that it is planned once.

findings.claim: Route 5 sends Lemma B.2 (finitely many étale covers of bounded degree) to IG.0 as a source. IG.0 plans only the construction of the profinite fundamental group from the fibre functor. Lemma B.2's proof needs three things. (i) The topological π₁ of a complex algebraic variety is finitely generated. (ii) Riemann existence (SGA 1 XII 5.1), which turns this into topological finite generation of the étale π₁. (iii) Invariance of π₁ under extension of algebraically closed fields in characteristic 0. The atlas plans Riemann existence at IG.3 (CHEN-24/112 is planned there, and so is Tau Ceti BelyiMaps layer 8). IG.3 depends on IG.1, which depends on IG.0. Placing Lemma B.2 at IG.0 therefore makes IG.0 consume a downstream layer, or makes the IG.0 blueprint plan Riemann existence a second time. The paper also uses Riemann existence in Lemma 5.8, to trivialise a finite monodromy group on a finite étale cover of the curve S. Item 22's note mentions that use, but no item carries Riemann existence at all.

findings.claim: Three slips in the source were seen but are not recorded in sourceIssues, as PROTOCOL §18 requires ('never silently corrected'). All three persist in the published text. (a) Remark 4.2 says the Betti map may be composed with 'a continuous group endomorphism of T^{2g}'. A non-injective endomorphism breaks Proposition 4.1(i) and (iii); 'automorphism' is meant, and the next sentence gives α ∈ GL_{2g}(ℤ). Item 25's note records this but no E does. (b) In the proof of Lemma 5.6, Grothendieck's theorem is applied to 'any element in Hom(B_s, A_s) ∩ Hom(H₁(B_s^an, ℤ), H₁(A_s^an, ℤ))'. Every homomorphism induces a ℤ-linear map on H₁, so this set is all of Hom(B_s, A_s), and the claim as printed is false. For a non-isotrivial elliptic scheme ℰ and B = ℰ_s × S, the identity of ℰ_s does not extend: an extension would be an isogeny on every fibre, making ℰ isotrivial. The π₁-equivariant homomorphisms are meant, as Deligne 4.1.3.2 states. Item 40 states the corrected form without an erratum. (c) Pages 19 and 21 attribute the Ax-type property to 'Ax's Theorem [2]' (Ax 1971, On Schanuel's conjectures). Page 6 cites '[3] for a constant abelian variety' (Ax 1972, analytic subgroups of algebraic groups) for the same input. Item 31's note records the inconsistency but no E does.
findings.evidence: arXiv v3 p.15 (published p.544): 'We remark that b from the proposition above is not unique as we can compose it with a continuous group endomorphism of T^{2g}. However, … we find b′ = α ∘ b for some α ∈ GL_{2g}(ℤ).' v3 p.25 (published p.556), checked on the page image: 'A theorem of Grothendieck [24] implies, that any element in Hom(B_s, A_s) ∩ Hom(H1(B_s^an, Z), H1(A_s^an, Z)) is induced by the restriction of a morphism ϕ: B → A over S to B_s'. v3 p.19 (published p.548): 'for the latter claim we refer to Ax's Theorem [2]'; v3 p.21 (published p.551): 'By Ax's Theorem [2], the set X is of Ax-type'; v3 p.6: 'and Ax's Theorem [3] for a constant abelian variety'; references: '2. J. Ax, On Schanuel's conjectures, Ann. of Math. (2) 93 (1971)'; '3. —, Some topics in differential algebraic geometry I: Analytic subgroups of algebraic groups, Amer. J. Math. 94 (1972)'. Item 25 note: 'Remark 4.2 says 'endomorphism' where 'automorphism' is meant.' Item 31 note: 'the paper cites [2] (Ax 1971) on pp.19 and 21 but [3] on p.6.' Item 40 statement: 'every homomorphism ℬ_s → 𝒜_s whose map on H₁ is monodromy-equivariant …'.

findings.claim: The proof of Lemma 5.2 first rescales so that y is real-analytic on (0,1). It then says that 'by looking at the proof of [30, Corollary 7.2(iii)] we may arrange γ(0) ∈ Γ and a(0) ∈ ℤⁿ'. Habegger–Pila's proof keeps β(0) ∈ Σ only before its last step. That step makes π₁∘β analytic on (0,1) by restarting at the first subinterval on which π₂∘β is non-constant, and it preserves only π₂(β(0)) ∈ π₂(Σ), which is what (iii) states. In Gao–Habegger's family, π₁ = (γ, a) and π₂ = y = γx − a. On the discarded initial interval y is constant while (γ(s), a(s)) may still move along solutions of (γ(s) − γ(0))x = a(s) − a(0). So the restarted point need not have γ ∈ Γ or a ∈ ℤⁿ, and the two requirements are not given together. The conclusion survives: by (iii), y(0) = y_{γ′} = γ′x − a_{γ′} for some γ′ ∈ Γ with H(γ′) ≤ T and a_{γ′} ∈ ℤⁿ. Hence exp(y(0)) = γ′·exp(x), and the Ax-type inclusion gives exp(x) + γ′^{-1}G′_x ⊆ γ′^{-1}(X) = X, which is all the proof uses. The review wrote the unsupported strengthening into item 30: 'it can be taken to start at one of the counted rational points; the paper needs γ(0) ∈ Γ and a(0) ∈ ℤⁿ'. LD.6 would then be asked to plan a statement that its source does not prove.

By looking at the proof of [30, Corollary 7.2(iii)] we may arrange γ(0) ∈ Γ and a(0) ∈ Z^n. Recall that X is of Ax-type. So there is a closed subgroup G′x ⊆ T^n with exp ∘ y([0, 1]) ⊆ exp(y(0)) + G′x ⊆ X. … We find exp(x) + Gx ⊆ γ(0)^{-1}(X) = X where Gx = γ(0)^{-1}G′x.' Habegger–Pila, arXiv 1409.0771v1 (the only arXiv version), Corollary 7.2(iii), p.23: 'We have π2(β(0)) ∈ π2(Σ).' The proof, p.25, gives 'β(0) = (y, z) ∈ Σ and (iii) follows', then: 'There exist 0 = a0 < a1 < ⋯ < ak+1 = 1 such that each π1 ∘ β|(ai,ai+1) … is real analytic. By continuity and (ii) the restriction of π2 ∘ β to some interval (ai, ai+1) is non-constant. If i is minimal with this property, then π2(β(ai)) = π2(β(0)) = z. This will preserve (iii) after a linear reparametrisation of (ai, ai+1) to (0, 1).' The Ann. Sci. ÉNS text of Habegger–Pila was not obtained (numdam served only a 6-page cover), so this is scoped to arXiv v1. findings.claim: Five general inputs of §§5–6 have no item and no cited owner. (a) Invariance of domain, used in Theorem 5.1 to make monodromy act on the components of Y_s meeting U. (b) The real constant-rank theorem, used in Lemma 6.2: the fibres of a maximal-rank-r map are manifolds of dimension 2 dim X − r. (c) The closed subgroups of Tⁿ are the annihilators of subgroups of ℤⁿ, so there are countably many, each 'defined globally by relations in integer coefficients' (Kronecker). This is used in Lemma 5.2 and Proposition 5.3. (d) The local theory of an irreducible complex analytic space, used in Propositions 5.3 and 5.4 and in Theorem 5.1: the smooth locus is dense and arcwise connected, the identity lemma holds, the dimension theory holds, and singular points of a one-dimensional analytic set are isolated. (e) Good covers of a Riemann surface (finite intersections empty or contractible, Weil), used to patch Betti maps in §5.2. PROTOCOL §16 asks for every key theorem the paper uses. The pinned libraries have Baire, which Lemma 5.2 also uses, but none of (a)–(e). The only atlas text near (d) is the draft SeveralComplexVariablesKahlerGeometry CV.1.

findings.claim: The file has no sourceVersions. Its only account of what was read, source.readSections, says 'The typeset Annals PDF was not accessible, so the published version was not collated.' The review then read and collated the published PDF, and every one of the 27 source issues cites the published version. So the record contradicts its own summary ('The independent review … collated the published Annals version'). A reader of source cannot tell which text the statements rest on. check_errata does not require the field here, because no finding quotes a stated result. collation.py infers 'published' only from the free-text 'searched' notes.
